A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 26 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including Appendices A-D, are readable and support comparison of the algorithms, proofs, table, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical algorithms, sample-complexity bounds, and proofs. Table 1 compares theoretical bounds; the MDP diagrams illustrate lower-bound constructions, not simulations.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The added 'Our focus' paragraph explicitly leaves empirical results for future work.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 adds two-fold subsampling before transition estimation and replaces its estimator's counts with trimmed counts. This changes data processing within the retained three-stage algorithm; exploration-policy construction and pessimistic planning remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical test scenarios. Both analyze the same finite-horizon tabular reward-agnostic and reward-free exploration problems.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. The methods compared through theoretical bounds in Table 1 are unchanged; newly cited works are not added to that comparison.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. The subsampling modification and revised sufficient sample counts concern the proposed algorithm and its theoretical guarantees.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses. The lower-bound constructions in Section 6 and Appendix C are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Changes to confidence-event allocation occur in theoretical proofs, rather than uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Concrete theoretical sample prescriptions change: Appendix B.2 replaces the coefficient 81·9440 with 81·75520, and Appendix B.4 replaces 81·28320 with 81·226560. These eightfold increases accompany subsampling; the remaining parameter factors and Table 1's asymptotic rates are unchanged. No empirical performance change is reported.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds the cited subsampling Lemma B.3 and a new retained-count proof in Lemma B.4. It revises the good events, replaces the Nμ/2 coverage threshold with Nμ/16, and updates both upper-bound proofs accordingly. This materially revises their probabilistic justification. Theorem 5.2 also changes its comparator from V^π to V*. The lower-bound proof remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction now qualifies the RFE upper-bound contribution as looser than Ménard et al. (2021) and included for theoretical completeness. The central claims of improved RAE lower-order complexity and a tight RFE lower bound remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits its focus to theoretical tabular MDP analysis and leaves non-tabular settings and empirical results for future work. Section 5 newly explains temporal dependence within trajectories and motivates subsampling as its remedy.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds instructions describing the main/auxiliary dataset split and count-based trimming. Appendix A.2 supplements its polynomial-time statement with Newton's method, problem dimensions, and a rough O(|S|^6|A|^3H^3) computational-cost estimate.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2022), Al-Marjani et al. (2023), Russo and Vannella (2024), and Russo and Pacchiano (2025) to its discussion of related exploration objectives. It also explicitly qualifies its RFE upper bound relative to Ménard et al. (2021). These are limited additions to the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The narrative gains focused paragraphs on related work, scope, subsampling, and computational cost, plus transitions around the new lemmas. The overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged; dates and some citation formatting also change.

P2.justification: Algorithm 3's displayed pseudocode expands, and algorithm blocks and Figures 1-2 shift with text reflow. Table 1 and both diagrams retain their contents and captions; there are no new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v1 asserts independence in its offline analysis after estimating transitions from complete trajectories. v2 explicitly addresses this issue with subsampling and retained-count lemmas, improving technical support and clarifying the contribution's scope. However, Algorithm 3 retains the all-N counting expression and returns D, while subsequent penalties still use unqualified counts. These inconsistencies limit the completeness of the correction, supporting a modest net improvement.
